Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 87, verse 1–7:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (1), Who created and proportioned (2), and Who determined and guided (3), and Who brought forth the pasture (4), then made it dark stubble (5). We shall make you recite, so you will not forget (6), except what God wills. Indeed, He knows what is manifest and what is hidden (7).﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is, "Magnify your Lord, the Most High, for there is no lord higher or greater than Him." Some of them, when they recited it, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

Mention of those who said that:

* Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Umar, that he used to recite: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾. He said: and it is so in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abd Khayr, who said: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recite: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, and he said: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasa, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, that Ibn Abbas, whenever he recited ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," and when he recited ﴿Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾ until he reached its end, ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, he would say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and yes."

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, whenever he recited it, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Dawud, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas recite in the maghrib prayer: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Exalt, O Muhammad, the name of your Lord, the Most High, by not naming anything else with it, forbidding him thereby from doing what the polytheists did in naming their deities, some of them al-Lat and some al-Uzza.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Exalt Allah above what the polytheists say about Him, as in His saying: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾. They said the meaning of that is: "Glorify your Lord, the Most High"; they said: the name is not intended here.

Others said: Exalt, O Muhammad, your mention of your Lord, the Most High, and your remembrance of Him, so that you do not mention Him except while you are humbly submissive to Him. They said: the "name" here is intended as the act of naming, but the word "name" was put in place of the verbal noun.

Others said: the meaning of His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ is: "Pray with the remembrance of your Lord, O Muhammad," meaning: "Pray while you are remembering Him," and from this comes "wajil" (fearful, anxious).

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the opinion of the one who said: its meaning is: Exalt the name of your Lord, that you not call upon idols and images with it, on account of what we have mentioned of the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from the Companions, that when they recited it they would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." Thereby it is made clear that its meaning was known to them: "Magnify and exalt the name of your Lord."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾

It means: He Who created things and perfected their creation, and made them balanced; and "taswiyah" is "ta'dil" (balancing, proportioning).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and Who determined and guided﴾

It means, may His remembrance be exalted: He Who determined the creation of things and guided them.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning intended by His saying: ﴿guided﴾. Some of them said: He guided man to the path of good and evil, and animals to their pastures.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning his saying: ﴿determined and guided﴾, he said: He guided man to misery and happiness, and guided the cattle to their pastures.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is that He guided males to the mating of females. We have already mentioned the report regarding that earlier.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that Allah, by His saying ﴿guided﴾, made the report general concerning His guidance of His creation, and did not specify any particular meaning over another. He has guided them to the path of good and evil, and guided males to the mating of females; so the report remains on its generality until there comes a report establishing proof, indicating its specificity. The readers of the great cities agreed on emphasizing the dal in ﴿qaddara﴾, except al-Kisa'i, who lightened it.

The correct reading in this is the emphasized form, because of the consensus of the proof upon it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and Who brought forth the pasture﴾

It means: He Who brought forth from the earth the pasture of the cattle, of various kinds of plants and types of herbage.

The interpreters said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yaqub ibn Makram related to me, he said: al-Hafari related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, ﴿brought forth the pasture﴾, he said: the plants.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿and Who brought forth the pasture...﴾, the verse: a plant, as you have seen, between yellow, red and white.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿then made it dark stubble﴾

It means, may His remembrance be exalted: He made that pasture into stubble, which is what has dried up from plants and withered, so that the wind carries it away. What is meant here is that He made it dry, brittle herbage, changed toward blackness (al-huwwa), which is blackness after whiteness or greenness, from the intensity of dryness.

The interpreters said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿dark stubble﴾, he said: brittle, changed herbage.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿dark stubble﴾, he said: the stubble of a torrent, dark, he said: black.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿dark stubble﴾, he said: it returns to dryness after greenness.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿then made it dark stubble﴾, he said: it was herbage and green plant, then it dried and withered, becoming dark stubble carried away by winds and torrents. But when it has a correct sense in its place, there is no way to seek to manipulate its meaning by preposing and postposing.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world, (16) while the Hereafter is better and more enduring. (17) Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, (18) the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. (19)﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, means: Successful is the one who purifies himself from disbelief and acts of disobedience to Allah, acts upon what Allah has commanded him, and performs His obligations.

A group of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: means, whoever purifies himself from polytheism.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari related to us, saying: Hisham related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: whoever's deeds are pure.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: he acts with piety (wara').

Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ikrima, regarding His saying: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: whoever says: There is no god but Allah.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Successful is the one who pays the zakat of his wealth.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu al-Ahwas, regarding ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: whoever is able to give a portion, let him do so, then let him stand and pray.

Muhammad ibn Imara al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu al-Ahwas, regarding ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: whoever gave a portion [[The report 172 is with the weak chain before it, and we have pointed to it there.]].

Muhammad ibn Imara related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Murra related to us, saying: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: When one of you is approached by a beggar while he intends to pray, let him put his zakat before his prayer, for Allah says: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾. So whoever is able to put zakat before his prayer, let him do so.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself﴾, he said: a man purifies himself by [giving] from his wealth, and pleases his Creator.

Others said: Rather, by this is meant the zakat al-fitr (charity at the end of Ramadan).

Mention of those who said that:

Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amali related to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya related to us, from Abu Khalada, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Aliya, and he said to me: When you go out tomorrow to the Eid, pass by me. So I passed by him, and he said: Have you eaten anything? I said: Yes. He said: Have you poured water over yourself? I said: Yes. He said: Tell me, what did you do with your zakat? I said: I have directed it. He said: That is all I wanted from you. Then he recited: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾, and said: The people of Madina do not regard any charity as more excellent than it and the giving of water (to drink).

* *

And His saying: ﴿and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: he affirms the oneness of Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾, he says: he affirms the oneness of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: he remembers Allah, calls upon Him, and turns to Him in desire.

The correct view on this is to say: he remembers Allah by affirming His oneness, calls upon Him, and turns to Him in desire, because all of that is remembrance of Allah, and Allah has not specified one kind of His remembrance over another.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and prays﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: what is meant is: he prays the five prayers.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and prays﴾, he says: he prays the five prayers.

Others said: what is meant is: the Eid prayer on the day of Fitr.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is: he remembers the name of his Lord and supplicates, and they said: the prayer here means supplication (du'a').

The correct view is to say: what is meant by His saying: ﴿and prays﴾ is the prayers, and the remembrance of Allah within them through glorification, exaltation and supplication.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world﴾

He says to the people: Nay, O people, you prefer the adornment of the life of this world over the Hereafter, ﴿while the Hereafter is better﴾ for you ﴿and more enduring﴾. He says: the adornment of the Hereafter is better for you, O people, and more enduring, because the life of this world is perishing, while the Hereafter is lasting, neither exhausted nor destroyed.

Something similar to what we have said has been said by the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world﴾: people chose the immediate, except those whom Allah protects.

* *

And His saying: ﴿while the Hereafter is better﴾

In goodness ﴿and more enduring﴾ in duration.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Abu Hamza related to us, from Ata', from Arfaja al-Thaqafi, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ to me. When he reached: ﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world﴾, he stopped reciting and turned to his companions and said: We preferred the world over the Hereafter. The people fell silent, and he said: We preferred the world because we saw its adornments, its women, its food and its drink, and the Hereafter was hidden from us, so we chose this immediate and left the deferred.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world﴾. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited ﴿Nay, you prefer﴾ with the letter ta', except Abu Amr, who recited it with the letter ya', and said: it means the wretched.

The recitation I do not prefer over this is with ta', due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it. It is also mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: ﴿Nay, you yourselves prefer﴾, and that too is evidence for the soundness of the recitation with ta'.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding what is referred to by His saying "this". Some of them said: it refers to the verses in ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾, he says: the verses that are in ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾.

Others said: the story of this surah.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾, he said: the story of this surah is in the former scriptures.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: that which Allah has related in this surah ﴿is in the former scriptures﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾, he said: that which Allah has related in this surah is in the former scriptures, ﴿the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾.

Others said: rather, what is meant is that His saying: ﴿while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ is in the former scriptures.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾, he said: the books of Allah succeeded one another, as you hear, that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾, he said: in the scriptures that Allah sent down to Abraham and Moses, that the Hereafter is better than the first.

The most correct of the sayings concerning this is the saying of the one who said: His saying: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays. Nay, you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and the scriptures of Moses son of Imran.

I only said that this is more correct than others, because "this" is a pointer to something present, so it is more fitting that it refers to what is nearest to it than to something else. As for "the scriptures" (al-suhuf), it is the plural of sahifa, and what is meant by it is the books of Abraham and Moses.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, from Abu al-Khalad, who said: The scriptures of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah was sent down six nights into Ramadan, the Psalms were sent down on the twelfth night, the Gospel was sent down on the eighteenth, and the Furqan was sent down on the twenty-fourth.

End of the commentary on the surah Sabbih isma rabbika al-A'la.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding what is referred to by His saying "this". Some of them said: it refers to the verses in ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾, he says: the verses that are in ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾.

Others said: the story of this surah.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾, he said: the story of this surah is in the former scriptures.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: that which Allah has related in this surah ﴿is in the former scriptures﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾, he said: that which Allah has related in this surah is in the former scriptures, ﴿the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾.

Others said: rather, what is meant is that His saying: ﴿while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ is in the former scriptures.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾, he said: the books of Allah succeeded one another, as you hear, that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾, he said: in the scriptures that Allah sent down to Abraham and Moses, that the Hereafter is better than the first.

The most correct of the sayings concerning this is the saying of the one who said: His saying: ﴿Successful is the one who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays. Nay, you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and the scriptures of Moses son of Imran.

I only said that this is more correct than others, because "this" is a pointer to something present, so it is more fitting that it refers to what is nearest to it than to something else. As for "the scriptures" (al-suhuf), it is the plural of sahifa, and what is meant by it is the books of Abraham and Moses.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, from Abu al-Khalad, who said: The scriptures of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah was sent down six nights into Ramadan, the Psalms were sent down on the twelfth night, the Gospel was sent down on the eighteenth, and the Furqan was sent down on the twenty-fourth.

End of the commentary on the surah Sabbih isma rabbika al-A'la.
